title: 2,000-Year-Old Kites: Inside the World's Kite Capital | China Travel Expert
description:
Over 2,000 years ago, one Chinese city sent the world's first kites into the sky — today it's the official World Capital of Kites.

Weifang in Shandong has been making kites for more than two millennia, and the craft peaked in the Ming dynasty. Weifang was named the Kite Capital in 1988, four years after it launched its International Kite Festival in 1984. Every April, hundreds of teams from dozens of countries fly here, and the city's signature is the giant dragon-head centipede kite — a chain of discs trailing a painted dragon head. The traditional craft has four skills: binding the bamboo frame, pasting the silk, painting it, and flying it.

🧭 Expert Tip: Time your visit for the International Kite Festival on the third Saturday of April, and buy a small Weifang "swallow" kite as a souvenir — they pack flat and actually fly.
